findings_and_connected_questions.classification: new current conditional source finding; aliases and central repair ownership unresolved
findings_and_connected_questions.title: Loot-to-target uses one party row instead of all same-item rows
findings_and_connected_questions.trace: The interface key describes Target as the quantity to retain or acquire in this inventory. The quest route loads party inventory rows and the party leader scoped targets; the template maps each loot item to the first same-item party row and puts only that quantity in data-current. The target-mode handler calculates target minus this one row and staged quantity. Stable physical objects can be represented as multiple quantity-1 rows with the same item ID. For example, if the party already holds two separate same-item rows of quantity 1 and the target is 2, the template supplies current=1 and the target-mode calculation can stage one more from a nonempty corresponding loot row, although the total of those party rows is already 2. This is arithmetic from source, not a run or simulated fixture.
findings_and_connected_questions.conditions: Requires this target to mean aggregate item quantity across the relevant party rows, qualifying stable objects and a same-item available loot row, and selection of target mode. Whether nested/conditioned items count in the intended target and the actual reachability, frequency, browser behavior and successful authoritative transfer remain unverified. The normal battle drop producer inspected at inventory_trade.rs:1361–1396 combines dropped quantities by item_id; duplicate loot-row staging is not asserted as reachable. Currency/alcohol/food grouping uses separate component controls in inventory-browser.js:218–299,302–350,380–444 and must be preserved; no blanket grouping claim.
findings_and_connected_questions.future_repair_direction: Reconcile the target owner and intended inclusion of physical, nested and measured objects, then compute the relevant aggregate safely and consistently with drafts and transfer admission. Preserve per-object identity, player choice, zero target behavior, and authoritatively validated transfers; any later verification waits for authorization.

findings_and_connected_questions.classification: newly assessed bounded cross-route evidence, narrows earlier conditional medical finding; not an independent broader-care finding
findings_and_connected_questions.trace: The quest page projects a live counterparty contact reference, membership revision, decision and limb. For a living counterparty, a limb and Request or EmergencyTreatment decision, the quest form sends the contact reference and expected membership revision; its distinct handler calls treat_limb with both Some values and the procedure fixed to Bandage. The ordinary surgery form has no claim fields and its handler sends None for both. The reducer accepts paired valid claims and contextual treatment requires a matching visible qualifying membership when one exists. Thus the earlier ordinary-surgery missing-claim finding does not imply all contextual treatment is unavailable: the quest bandage route is a distinct path that supplies that pair.
findings_and_connected_questions.conditions: The form and forwarding demonstrate source intent only. Successful treatment still depends on living characters, co-presence, exact visible current membership, permission or emergency, admission and other reducer preconditions. This narrow contrast does not show general procedures are available by the quest bandage form or that any runtime treatment succeeded.
findings_and_connected_questions.future_repair_direction: When reconciling the earlier ordinary-surgery case, carry the authoritative context/revision as appropriate without conflating the separate Bandage-only quest action, refusal, emergency, retry and stale-revision decisions.

findings_and_connected_questions.classification: bounded unresolved contracts, not established defect or security claim
findings_and_connected_questions.trace: The mission page embeds mission_id in a Datastar expression and native path and addr in a native query; the typed MissionId constructor restricts validated values to bounded canonical lowercase ASCII and tactical request/claim paths call it. The canonical CaseSiteId constructor similarly disallows slash and query delimiters, narrowing concern for the case-site autoresolve path. Case-site presentation action_id may instead be a contract or battle ID for loot, whose full admission and route contract are not established by this read. The value display maps missing catalog/base_value to zero while weight displays a dash; interface help dash language specifically discusses weapon and armor measurement columns. The template compares victor to an enemies literal while core has a separate StrategicBattleVictor enum, but producer mapping and business semantics were not traced.
findings_and_connected_questions.conditions: No proof that all mission views originate in the checked producer paths, that published server addresses satisfy query-encoding assumptions, that missing base_value means unknown rather than zero, or that the victor producers use the existing enum in this presentation. HTML escaping is not itself evidence of correct JavaScript or URL component encoding. No browser, service or injection probe performed.
findings_and_connected_questions.future_repair_direction: Trace actual admission and framework-native encoders/consumers and catalog/victor owners before deciding type/escaping/error changes. Preserve intended path semantics and distinguish unknown from numeric zero only when native value policy establishes that meaning.

nonfindings.text: The separate quest Bandage handler does pass both contextual claim components; it does not make all ordinary surgery forms correct or prove treatment success.

Under the inspected tactical admissions, MissionId excludes quotes, slashes and query markers; canonical CaseSiteId also excludes slash and query delimiters. The whole source graph and alternative inputs remain unproved; do not infer an injection exploit from raw interpolation alone.
The guarded treatment_limb_slug unwrap_or_default occurs only in an is_some branch in this template; no missing-limb default reaches this form under ordinary source control flow.

The inspected normal battle-drop producer combines item IDs before inserting loot, so a multiple-loot-row staging scenario is not established by this producer. Separate party object rows are explicitly admitted.
The missing-price observation is not resolved by the help text alone: its dash sentence names weapon and armor measurement columns, and base_value meaning remains open.
Mission status branches on MissionStatus, ready connection requires Some character_id, and pending state supplies a cancel form. None of those establish live readiness or successful enrollment.
Quantity and price are converted to u64 before multiplication in the loot/party display; multiplying two u32 values fits in u64.

open_questions: Which physical, nested, measured and condition-specific items count toward a party item target, and should staging across multiple UI rows share one item-level remaining deficit?
Do canonical address and action ID sources and URL/Datastar consumer contracts cover every actual admitted path and query?
Does absent catalog/base_value represent unknown, zero or another policy; what is the owner for autoresolve victor and corpse location values?
What user-visible outcome and retry semantics apply to cancellation, loot transfer and ordinary surgery, and what historical first-cut aliases are exact?
How does central reconciliation connect 059 q188/q629 pair parsing, q546 target acknowledgement, q1885 context/victor questions and the new aggregate finding without conflation?
